title: Optimal Confidence Sets for Ordinal Complier Pairwise Effects with Vanishing Complier Share
banked_reason: The central unknown-mass connected-interval problem remains unsolved: the note proves only existence and asymptotic convergence of a generic discretization scheme, without an exact value, a 10^(-4) primal-dual bracket, or an explicit attaining rule.
gap_reasons: The promised sharp unknown-mass connected-interval deliverable is still explicitly open: no exact value, attaining rule, or outward-rounded continuum primal/dual certificate with the required 1e-4 gap is supplied; the existence/convergence handle and nonmatching bounds do not make the weak-stratum interval usable as the advertised sharp rule.

The union ranges over an unspecified pilot outcome-law region, not explicitly its intersection with mathcalF; it can contain F' with q_{F',-}(u)=0, so WR_n need not be a compact finite ratio interval and the loss-floor argument cannot apply.
proof_attempt_summary: Two D0 rounds developed a weighted known-mass Pratt rule, a curvature-based strict lower bound, and a causal transfer argument. The exact unknown-mass connected-interval optimizer or certified 1e-4 continuum bracket remained open, so D0.5 graded the delivered package incremental against the field floor. The ratio-image construction also has a domain defect, and the attested EHS excerpt does not by itself establish the full Neyman-Pearson lemma as stated; repair both before reusing those claims.
tldr: Ordinal complier pairwise effects leave the regular regime when the complier fraction is of order \(n^{-1/2}\). In the resulting Gaussian experiment, the paper derives an exact shifted weighted-Pratt rule for every continuously differentiable strictly increasing target with positive derivative, even against arbitrary randomized measurable confidence sets. A non-midpoint balance anchor creates a strictly positive radial-nuisance lower bound already in that broad action class; for the causal quadratic, the anchor is displaced exactly when curvature is nonzero, while affine targets have zero unknown-mass cost. For the unknown-mass connected-interval game the paper proves optimizer existence and convergence of a certifiable primal-dual approximation, but the exact value, explicit attaining rule, and \(10^{-4}\) certificate remain open. The abstract connected minimax value transfers uniformly to observable causal data, and a common-composition curve gives joint win, loss, and win-ratio coverage.
gap: Regular PGCE influence-function theory divides by the square of a principal-stratum probability and does not remain uniform when the complier fraction is of order \(n^{-1/2}\). Expected-measure theory solves bounded location problems, but its pointwise test inversion does not solve a connected-interval game with radial nuisance and a curved scalar target.
fill: The project proves an affine-versus-curved if-and-only-if frontier, certifies the known-mass benchmark, solves the connected unknown-mass saddle problem, and transfers its value and attaining rule uniformly to observable causal data without deleting the endpoint baseline channels.
